prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational, precise exercise-phase edit.
Create the matching FINISH of Reverse-Grip (SUPINATED / underhand) FRONT Lat Pulldown.

IMAGE 1 is the user-selected START master. Preserve its exact man, face/hair, physique, blue-gray shirt, charcoal shorts, white socks and gray trainers; same seated hips, legs, shoes, thigh-pad contacts, whole machine, camera, crop, white background and lighting. Preserve the SAME chrome long bar, central swivel/carabiner and its knurled straight inner sections. This is a paired frame, not a redesign.
IMAGE 2 is ONLY a guide for the corrected eight-raised/twelve-resting weight stack and the lengthened cable during FINISH. It depicts a DIFFERENT wide overhand grip. Never copy image 2's wide hand positions, forearm rotation, shoulder-abducted pose or overhand grip.

MOVEMENT:
The exact bar from image 1 now descends IN FRONT of the face to the upper chest / upper sternum, just below the chin. Never behind the neck. Both hands retain image 1's SAME comfortable near-shoulder-width placement on the STRAIGHT INNER sections, with the angled outer bar ends extending unused on each side. The central collar remains between the hands and physically centered. Do not shorten or reshape the bar to make it fit.
Both hands remain SUPINATED: the palms face the athlete's face/chest, as in an underhand chin-up, not forward toward the tower and not facing each other. Anatomically true left and right hands, four curled fingers and opposing wrapped thumbs, proportional palms and natural knuckles. Wrists continue their forearms without a sharp backward or lateral kink. No hand switching between phases. Preserve natural perspective and allow partial occlusion rather than separately twisting hands to face the camera.
Both elbows bend, descend and travel relatively close to the sides of the torso, not flared out like the wide grip. Elbows finish below shoulder level near the torso, without being dragged far behind the back. Forearms aim naturally upward from these lowered elbows to the inner bar grips. Upper arms stay naturally attached and have plausible lengths.
Torso retains image 1's modest stable backward inclination, with no extra recline to pull the load. Chest comfortably lifted, ribcage over pelvis, natural spine. No torso twist, exaggerated lumbar arch or head jutting forward. Shoulder blades move naturally down/back with the pull without forced over-squeezing or shrugging. Hips remain fully seated, thighs under rollers, both knees and feet EXACTLY in image 1's positions.

PERSPECTIVE:
Bar remains in front of the upper chest. In this side/rear camera, the nearer arm, shoulder or torso may partly hide the far hand/bar; preserve that honest occlusion. Do not put the shaft across the nape to show it. Entire bar, body, seat and tower use the SAME 3D axes.

MECHANICS:
Same high pulley at the original boom exit. One longer taut straight cable runs to the black stop ball, cable terminal and ONE closed carabiner through the bar's single central eyelet. Center collar at the bar midpoint, no floating connector, duplicated chain or cable intersecting skin.
The START master has TWENTY weight plates, with the yellow selector in the eighth from the top. Show exactly EIGHT selected upper plates raised together, the single yellow pin in the BOTTOM/eighth raised plate, and exactly TWELVE stationary plates remaining on the original lower base. Empty gap immediately below the selected pin plate; no extra plate beneath it. Use image 2's corrected eight-plus-twelve construction, not its arm pose. Never increase the total plate count or move the stationary stack off its base. Continuous silver guide rods, coherent moving pulley, rigid unchanged frame.

Output one full portrait FINISH only, same CRESUM premium semi-realistic 3D studio style. Natural anatomy, skin, detailed grip contact and clothing folds caused by the lowered arms. No text, logos, arrows, inset or muscle overlays. Key requirement: genuine bilateral underhand grip at unchanged INNER hand positions, elbows down relatively close to the body, bar near the upper chest IN FRONT of the athlete, stable lower body.
